name: The Postmortem Tournament
author: SHIP IT core
description: Five rounds of live incidents in front of a scoreboard. Rival teams are playing the same gauntlet; your postmortems are scored on speed (MTTR), honesty (corrective actions) and follow-through (credits claimed, restores proven). Finish first.

missions.title: Registration desk
missions.story: The conference banner goes up in the audit feed: POSTMORTEM TOURNAMENT — ROUND ONE OPENS SHORTLY. Three rival teams are on the board: Cloud Nine, Null Pointers, Ping Payments. The rules are one line: incidents will happen. What you write after them is the score.
missions.objective: A traffic surge is coming. Resolve it, then file the postmortem with at least two corrective actions — inside 150 sim minutes of it opening.
missions.coaching: Surges self-resolve when the traffic dies down; autoscaling and enough replicas shorten the pain. Then MONITORING → INCIDENTS → postmortem: tick the actions you actually did. The scoreboard (MODES tab) is live.
hints: The surge opens ~10 sim minutes after the round starts. It resolves itself when the spike ends — your job is to be READY: enough replicas, then watch.
The moment it resolves: MONITORING → INCIDENTS → the surge → FILE POSTMORTEM. Tick at least two corrective actions (autoscale, traffic alert, capacity).
The clock is the MTTR requirement — 150 sim minutes from incident open to resolution. If it is dragging, check that nothing is starving capacity.

onStart.audit: TOURNAMENT ROUND 1: a large account is about to hammer the orders API. Clock starts when it opens.

missions.title: Round of eight: the rollback
missions.story: Round two, and the organizers stop pretending: someone on YOUR team ships a broken release to production while you watch. The scoreboard does not care whose commit it was. It cares how fast the blast radius shrinks.
missions.objective: A bad deploy is coming (~10 sim minutes). Roll it back and file the postmortem with three corrective actions — MTTR inside 90 minutes.
missions.coaching: CI tab → the latest deployment → ROLLBACK. That is the whole skill: deciding in seconds what took your users hours. Then the postmortem: rollback, error alert, staging gate.

requirements.label: The bad deploy was rolled back and resolved
MTTR ≤ 90 sim minutes (blast radius shrinks fast)

hints: The error spike lands ~10 sim minutes in. CI tab → DEPLOYMENTS → the newest one → ROLLBACK. Do not debug in production what you can undo in one click.
90 minutes MTTR — the clock starts when the incident opens, and the rollback is instant once you click. The postmortem can follow after.
Three corrective actions: roll back, error-rate alert, staging/e2e gate before prod. Tick what is true.

onStart.audit: TOURNAMENT ROUND 2: a teammate is about to ship a broken release. The scoreboard does not care whose commit it was.

missions.title: Semifinal: their outage, your pager
missions.story: Semifinal. The organizers schedule a REGION-WIDE PROVIDER OUTAGE and call it a level playing field — every team gets the same outage. You cannot fix it. You can still be the team that reads the status page, banks the credit and writes the honest postmortem.
missions.objective: Survive the provider outage (~15 sim minutes from now), claim the SLA credit, and file the postmortem with two corrective actions.
missions.coaching: Provider outages resolve themselves; the credit window is a sim day. CLOUD → Providers → REQUEST SLA CREDIT after it ends. Postmortem: status-page check, credit claimed, provider comparison.
hints: Everything drops to ~80% errors for 15–45 sim minutes and NOTHING you own is broken. Check the incident detail: it says provider-side. Ride it out.
When it ends: CLOUD → Providers → REQUEST SLA CREDIT. Providers pay for their own outages — if you ask. The claim lands in the incident timeline (that is what the scoreboard checks).
Then the postmortem: status page first, credit claimed, evaluate a more reliable provider. The honest postmortem beats the heroic one.

onStart.audit: TOURNAMENT SEMIFINAL: your provider's region is about to have a very bad day. Same outage for every team.

missions.title: Final four: drop the database
missions.story: The organizers have stopped being subtle: they drop your ORDERS TABLE. In front of everyone. This is the round that separates the teams with backups from the teams with opinions about backups.
missions.objective: Restore the orders table from YOUR backup — RTO ≤ 150 sim minutes — and file the postmortem with three corrective actions.
missions.coaching: CLOUD → Databases → RESTORE FROM BACKUP (point-in-time picks the last snapshot before the drop — that only works if backups were enabled BEFORE now). Verify rows in the DATABASE tab, then postmortem.

requirements.label: MTTR ≤ 150 sim minutes from the drop

hints: The drop lands ~10 sim minutes in. If automated backups are on, a snapshot from yesterday exists — the restore is one button (CLOUD → Databases).
RTO is measured from incident open: every minute you spend reading chat is a minute of RTO. Restore first, feel things later.
Verify ≥900k rows in the DATABASE tab (\dt or SELECT count-ish), then postmortem: backups, restore drill, PITR/retention.

onStart.audit: TOURNAMENT FINAL FOUR: they are about to drop your orders table. Backups or opinions — pick one now.

missions.title: The trophy
missions.story: No incident this round. Just the scoreboard, the rivals, and the question the tournament actually asks: when the pager fires, is your team the one that recovers, documents and gets billed correctly? Points decide. So do the last few minutes of calm.
missions.objective: Clear the scoreboard round: no open incidents, all four rounds won, and tournament points ≥ 38 — ahead of every rival team.
missions.coaching: The MODES tab shows live standings. If a rival is ahead, the only lever left is speed on any remaining rounds — points come from winning them fast.
hints: Resolve anything still open — the trophy round requires a calm board (no open incidents).
Points come from the four rounds (8+10+10+12 = 40). If you were slow somewhere, the rivals may have caught up — check the MODES tab standings.
Nothing else to do: no open incidents, 4 rounds, ≥38 points. Collect the trophy.
